source.name: North American Amphibian Monitoring Program (NAAMP) anuran detection data

ecological_question: Do short-term weather pulses increase the number and alter the identity of frog species calling together during the same standardized listening event?

hypotheses.H1: warm/wet survey conditions increase event-level co-calling richness
hypotheses.H2: recent rainfall has a stronger synchronizing association than temperature where directly recorded
hypotheses.H3: weather synchrony is strongest near seasonal shoulders
hypotheses.H4: weather pulses transiently densify event-level co-calling networks

cannot_claim: first evidence that temperature or rainfall affects frog calling
first evidence of acoustic niche partitioning
first observation that frog species can co-call
prior_art_boundary.target_novelty: weather-dependent dynamic synchrony of standardized multi-species calling assemblages

allowed_structural_reads: ScienceBase file names sizes hashes and media types
tabular headers and documented field definitions
route stop survey date and event identifiers
call-index field names and missingness indicators without opening associations
weather temperature rainfall wind sky field names and missingness indicators
counts of events represented by records for two or more species solely as estimability
forbidden_before_freeze: weather variable selected by p value or model fit
network edges selected for biological interpretation
